name: Seamsplit — Augment-Integrated Haute Couture
creator: House Seamsplit, founded by designer Mirembe Castillo-Johanssen, Tier 4, 2211
description: A luxury fashion house and movement that designs garments as functional extensions of the wearer's augmentation — fabric that routes through port housings, sleeves that interface directly with arm chrome and display its operational data as woven light patterns, structural elements that redistribute mechanical joint load, collars that integrate with neural port architecture. Seamsplit pieces require a full augmentation survey before fabrication and are unique to each wearer's specific chrome configuration. Each piece costs between Φ15,000 and Φ200,000 and cannot be worn by anyone else.
cultural_impact: Seamsplit redefined luxury fashion in M88 by making the body's augmentation history the irreducible core of the garment — a piece that cannot be copied, re-sold, or worn by another person is a fundamentally different luxury object than anything that came before. The movement also forced a conversation about fashion as prosthetic, blurring the line between clothing and medical device.
controversy: Seamsplit's collection for a Spire-tier corporate security executive was revealed to incorporate tactical augmentation integration — essentially camouflaged weapons-system clothing — leading to a brief regulatory crisis about what constitutes a garment versus an armament. The house settled without admitting wrongdoing.
story_hooks: A Seamsplit piece belonging to a murdered Spire executive contains embedded logs of every location the garment has been — and the house's designer knows exactly how to read them.
A black-market Seamsplit knockdown operation is producing cheap imitations that interface incorrectly with the wearer's augmentation, causing cascading neural failures.

Mirembe Castillo-Johanssen is commissioned to design a piece for someone whose augmentation configuration suggests they are not who they claim to be — the designer must decide whether to complete the commission or report what they've seen.
